```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6,
                      fig.height = 3.5)
```

`hcesfort` estimates apparent micronutrient intake from a Household
Consumption and Expenditure Survey (HCES) and models what fortifying a food
would change. This vignette runs the whole chain on `hces_example`, a
synthetic survey: every value is invented and it describes no country.

```{r library}
library(hcesfort)
ex <- hces_example
names(ex)
```

## 1. From acquisitions to apparent intake

Quantities are converted to grams, linked to the composition of the
**unfortified** foods, and divided by the adult female equivalents (AFE) of
each household.

```{r intake}
nutrients <- nutrient_registry(ex$nutrients)
grams <- convert_units(ex$acquisitions, ex$unit_factors, priority = "food")
baseline <- unfortified_baseline(ex$composition, ex$enrichment, nutrients)
afe <- adult_equivalents(
  ex$members,
  reference_kcal = reference_energy("female", 25, 55, pal = 1.76),
  weight_kg = c(female = 55, male = 65), pal = 1.76
)
content <- link_composition(grams, ex$crosswalk, baseline)
intake <- apparent_intake(content, afe, ex$households)
head(intake[intake$intake_status == "estimated", 1:6], 3)
```

Every step records what it received, excluded or flagged:

```{r audit}
audit_summary(intake)
```

## 2. Fortification scenarios

`vehicle_coverage()` measures how much of each vehicle a household acquires;
`apply_scenario()` adds the nutrients that a scenario would put in it.

```{r scenario}
use <- vehicle_coverage(grams, ex$vehicles, afe, ex$households)
scenarios <- apply_scenario(intake, use, ex$scenarios,
                            compliance_model = "average_content")
unique(scenarios$scenario)
```

## 3. Inadequacy and its uncertainty

The probability of inadequacy of each household is averaged with the survey
design. Estimates come with an interval and are judged by the presentation
standard before they are shown.

```{r risk}
iron <- ref_iron_requirements
iron <- iron[iron$group == "females_menstruating_adult", ]
risk <- inadequacy(
  scenarios, ref_requirements, distribution = list(iron = iron),
  bioavailability = list(iron = 0.10), min_coverage = 0.8,
  min_records_used = 0.8
)
design <- as_hces_design(ex$households, lonely_psu = "adjust")
folate <- risk[risk$nutrient == "folate", ]
by_group <- estimate_households(
  design, folate, "p_inadequate", by = "expenditure_group",
  ci_method = "korn_graubard"
)
by_group <- flag_presentation(by_group)
head(by_group[c("scenario", "expenditure_group", "estimate", "ci_low",
                "ci_high", "n", "presentation")], 5)
```

## 4. One figure by domain

The functions return tidy tibbles, so any figure is a `ggplot2` call. Here
the folate inadequacy in each expenditure group, before and after one
scenario. Estimates that the standard suppresses are left out.

```{r figure, eval = requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)}
library(ggplot2)
shown <- by_group[by_group$presentation != "suppress" &
                    by_group$scenario %in% c("baseline", "wheat_flour"), ]
ggplot(shown, aes(expenditure_group, estimate, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = ci_low, ymax = ci_high),
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.4)) +
  labs(x = "Expenditure group", y = "Probability of inadequacy (folate)",
       colour = "Scenario") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Reports in the shape of the results of an analysis (readiness and results)
are generated with `use_report_template()`.
